To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HRM metrics are used to evaluate the success of new HRM practices.
the use of metrics in HRM can be effective and that the use of customer, employee, and financial metrics can be effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how HRM metrics can be used to demonstrate the value added of HRM.
the use of data‐and metrics‐driven approaches to HRM.
the following question: Can HRM practices be evaluated using scientific measures?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of scientific measures and metrics to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of human resource management practices is not a new idea.
the use of metrics and measures in HRM practices is a very useful tool to evaluate the success of HRM practices.
HRM is a strategic business partner and should be measured and evaluated in a way that is consistent with the way other business partners are measured and evaluated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of metrics in HRM is an important step in the evolution of the profession.
the use of metrics in the HRM function can provide a powerful tool for demonstrating the effectiveness of HR practices.
we have demonstrated how metrics can be used in the evaluation of human resource management projects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HRM can use data‐driven approaches to evaluate its practices and to demonstrate its impact.
the use of data‐driven metrics can help HRM to be viewed as a value‐adding function.
HRM practices can and should be measured and evaluated using metrics.
